code_label: Quantum ideas can enhance financial forecasting
text_span: we show how quantum machine learning can be used to improve financial forecasting
rationale: States the paper’s central aim and claimed contribution.

code_label: DPP-RF improves churn precision
text_span: improving precision by almost 6%
rationale: Summarizes the main churn prediction result.

code_label: QNNs match classical performance with fewer parameters
text_span: match classical performance with significantly fewer parameters
rationale: Summarizes the main credit risk result.

code_label: Quantum ideas can help today and later
text_span: both today as quantum-inspired classical ML solutions, and even more in the future, with the advent of better quantum hardware
rationale: Frames the present and future relevance of the approach.

code_label: Two finance use cases at Itaú
text_span: focusing on two use cases within the business of Itaú Unibanco
rationale: Defines the application scope of the study.

code_label: DPP sampling used to enhance Random Forests
text_span: We introduce quantum algorithms for Determinantal Point Processes (DPP) sampling, and develop a method of DPP sampling to enhance Random Forest models.
rationale: Describes the first methodological contribution.

code_label: Classical DPP outperforms baseline on key metrics
text_span: the proposed algorithms outperform the baseline Random Forest in precision, efficiency, and bottom line
rationale: States the claimed classical DPP-RF advantage.

code_label: Quantum processor works only on small batches
text_span: The quantum algorithm run on an IBM quantum processor gives similar results as the classical DPP on small batch dimensions but falters as the dimensions grow bigger due to hardware noise.
rationale: States a hardware-related limitation of the quantum experiment.

code_label: Orthogonality reduces redundancy
text_span: add the property of orthogonality for the trained model weights to avoid redundancy in the learned features
rationale: Explains the motivation for orthogonal layers.

code_label: Compound networks explore exponential space
text_span: compound neural network architectures that are appropriate for financial data
rationale: Introduces the second model family used in the paper.

code_label: DPP-RF uses diverse subsampling
text_span: utilizes Determinantal Point Processes (DPPs) instead of uniform sampling to subsample rows and columns
rationale: Defines the core algorithmic change to Random Forest.

code_label: DPPs promote diversity and correct bias
text_span: DPP sampling better preserves the diversity of the dataset, and corrects for sampling bias
rationale: States the intended statistical benefit of DPP sampling.

code_label: DPPs can yield unbiased least-squares estimates
text_span: we get an unbiased estimate of w∗
rationale: Presents a theoretical property motivating the method.

code_label: Classical DPP sampling remains costly
text_span: The naive sampling method — calculating all subdeterminants and performing l2 sampling — takes exponential time.
rationale: Identifies computational difficulty of exact DPP sampling.

code_label: Quantum DPP sampling may reduce complexity
text_span: Recent work has shown that quantum computers are in principle able to sample from DPPs in even lower complexity in some cases.
rationale: States the potential quantum advantage claim with hedging.

code_label: Novel batched DPP-RF procedure
text_span: a novel sampling procedure was developed which preserves many of the benefits of DPPs, but does not require sampling from the full dataset
rationale: Describes the practical workaround used for large data.

code_label: Churn prediction target and horizon
text_span: predict which customers are most likely to churn in the next three months using customer data from the previous six months
rationale: Defines the prediction task and temporal setup.

code_label: Churn dataset size and split
text_span: The primary dataset used in this study consists of 304,000 datapoints, with 153 features for each datapoint.
rationale: Provides the scale of the churn dataset.

code_label: Business goal is high-precision intervention
text_span: The focus of this exploration was to reduce false positives in the flagged customers to increase the efficiency of bank interventions.
rationale: States the operational objective driving model tuning.

code_label: Precision improved at low recall
text_span: our method showed an improvement in precision from 71.6% for the benchmark model to 77.5% with the new model
rationale: Reports the main churn classification improvement.

code_label: DPP-RF training is slower than baseline
text_span: it took 54 minutes to train the model with the best hyperparameters using, compared to 311 seconds for the benchmark model
rationale: States the runtime tradeoff of the proposed method.

code_label: Batch size strongly affects runtime
text_span: The training time of a DPP-RF model depends heavily on this batch size parameter
rationale: Identifies a key hyperparameter affecting feasibility.

code_label: DPP-RF improves withdrawals captured
text_span: the BM model captures 61.42% of the total, whilst the DPP-RF model captures 62.77%
rationale: Reports the business KPI improvement.

code_label: DPP-RF improves maximum possible withdrawals captured
text_span: the BM model captures 69.18% of the total, whilst the DPP-RF model captures 70.72%
rationale: Reports the second business KPI improvement.

code_label: OpenML benchmarks show mixed gains
text_span: The results are reported via the ROC-AUC metric.
rationale: Introduces the benchmark evaluation framework and comparative results.

code_label: Quantum DPP circuit has lower theoretical complexity
text_span: a quantum computer can more natively perform DPP sampling, achieving a gate complexity of O(nd) and a circuit depth of O(d log(n))
locator: 4.1 Quantum Circuits for Determinantal Point Processes
rationale: States the claimed quantum complexity advantage.

code_label: Hardware experiment required problem reduction
text_span: we had to reduce the size of our problem
rationale: States the practical constraint imposed by available hardware.

code_label: Quantum hardware-ready pipeline uses PCA and small batches
text_span: Applying PCA to reduce the number of columns from 153 to d = 2, 3;
rationale: Describes the dimensionality reduction step for hardware execution.

code_label: IBM processor matches simulator only on small dimensions
text_span: for small matrix dimensions — up to (6,2) — the IBM quantum processor gives results similar to the ones achieved with the simulator
rationale: Summarizes the hardware-vs-simulator comparison.

code_label: Hardware noise worsens larger DPP samples
text_span: as the dimensions grow bigger, the samples from the quantum DPP circuits lead to worse classifier performance
rationale: States the observed degradation with larger circuits.

code_label: Quantum neural networks use orthogonal and compound layers
text_span: we use quantum neural networks with orthogonal and compound layers
locator: 5.1 Quantum Neural Networks with Orthogonal and Compound Layers
rationale: Defines the second major model family.

code_label: Orthogonal layers reduce redundancy and vanishing gradients
text_span: it reduces the redundancy in the trained weights and can avoid the age-old problem of vanishing gradients
locator: 5.1 Quantum Neural Networks with Orthogonal and Compound Layers
rationale: States the expected benefit of orthogonality.

code_label: Unary, RY, and H data loaders
text_span: we define a different technique for loading the data in the entire 2d-dimensional Hilbert space
rationale: Introduces the data-loading strategies used in the QNNs.

code_label: RBS gates preserve hamming weight
text_span: RBS gates and circuits preserve the hamming weight of the input state
rationale: Explains the structural property underlying the layers.

code_label: Compound layers act on all fixed hamming-weight subspaces
text_span: the k-th block of this unitary applies a compound matrix of order k of the n × n unary matrix
rationale: Describes how compound layers generalize orthogonal layers.

code_label: Pyramid circuit is fully expressive for orthogonal matrices
text_span: the pyramid circuit expresses exactly the Special Orthogonal Group
rationale: States the expressivity claim for the circuit architecture.

code_label: Backpropagation training is polynomial for orthogonal layers
text_span: This backpropagation method for the pyramid circuit ... takes time O(n2)
rationale: Reports the training complexity advantage.

code_label: Expectation-per-subspace layer compresses exponential output
text_span: one can still try to use a loss function that contains some information about the distribution
rationale: Explains the rationale for the custom compound-layer loss.

code_label: Credit risk dataset and KPI
text_span: we are interested in calculating the so-called probability of default (PD)
locator: 6.1 Use Case Introduction: Credit Risk Prediction
rationale: Defines the credit-risk prediction target.

code_label: Gini score used as main KPI
text_span: the main Key Performance Indicator (KPI) that we use is the Gini score
locator: 6.1 Use Case Introduction: Credit Risk Prediction
rationale: States the evaluation metric for the credit model.

code_label: SME dataset size and split
text_span: The dataset used consists of ≈141, 500 observations, each one represented by 32 features
locator: 6.1 Use Case Introduction: Credit Risk Prediction
rationale: Provides the scale of the credit-risk dataset.

code_label: Residual, orthogonal, and compound architectures compared
text_span: We designed three neural network architectures.
locator: 6.2 Neural Network Architectures for Credit Risk
rationale: Introduces the comparative model setup.

code_label: Orthogonal and compound layers use far fewer parameters
text_span: these new layers learn the angles of 2n RBS gates instead of n2 elements of the weight matrix
rationale: Highlights the parameter-efficiency finding.

code_label: OrthoResNN matches baseline Gini
text_span: OrthoResNN ... 54.29%
rationale: Reports the orthogonal model’s test performance.

code_label: ExpResNN slightly underperforms OrthoResNN
text_span: ExpResNN ... 53.95%
rationale: Reports the compound model’s test performance.

code_label: Public benchmarks show small differences
text_span: The results are summarised in Table 5.
rationale: Introduces the benchmark comparison across datasets.

code_label: Quantum inference on hardware uses trained classical parameters
text_span: Both neural networks were trained classically, and the trained parameters were used to construct our quantum circuits for inference.
rationale: Describes the hybrid training/inference setup.

code_label: Hardware inference limited to small subsample
text_span: we decided to perform inference using the trained models on a small test subsample of 300 test points
rationale: States the hardware capacity constraint.

code_label: OrthoResNN hardware result below noiseless simulation
text_span: the inference yielded a Gini score of 50.19%
rationale: Reports the noisy hardware performance for the orthogonal model.

code_label: ExpFNN hardware result much worse than simulation
text_span: which yielded a Gini score of 40.20%
rationale: Reports the noisy hardware performance for the compound model.

code_label: Orthogonal layer is more NISQ-friendly
text_span: This remarkable result underscores the NISQ-friendliness of the orthogonal layer
locator: 7.2 Improving the Hardware Results with Error Mitigation Techniques
rationale: Interprets the hardware findings as evidence of NISQ suitability.

code_label: Error mitigation closes most of the hardware gap
text_span: we were able to achieve a Gini score of 53.68% for the OrthoResNN
locator: 7.2 Improving the Hardware Results with Error Mitigation Techniques
rationale: Reports the mitigated hardware improvement.

code_label: Mitigation techniques add overhead and may not scale
text_span: Some of these techniques are based on heuristics and/or do not have efficient scaling at larger circuit sizes.
locator: 7.2 Improving the Hardware Results with Error Mitigation Techniques
rationale: States an explicit caveat about mitigation scalability.

code_label: Quantum ideas can be turned into classical ML today
text_span: Performance enhancements can be achieved today by turning these quantum ideas into classical ML solutions run on GPUs.
rationale: Summarizes the paper’s present-day practical claim.

code_label: Better hardware may improve speed and results
text_span: with the advent of better quantum hardware, we expect these methods to run faster and produce even better results
rationale: States the forward-looking expectation for quantum hardware.
